title: MAP DATA
description:
In addition to publishing seven daily headline indices comprised of more than 130 individual assessments, the Baltic Exchange also produces FFA forward curves for all listed products, options' volatilies and volume data.

 

Additional products include the Baltic Sale and Purchase Assessments (BSPA), the Baltic Ship Recycling Assessments (BRSA) and the Baltic Cost of Operating Index (BOPEX).

segments.title: Air
segments.description:
The Baltic Exchange Airfreight Index (BAI) – powered by TAC data – reflects the price per kilogram of general cargo flown on 17 key tradelanes, from origin airport to destination region.

General cargo includes high value goods, such as electronics, jewellery and pharmaceuticals. Transport by air is critical for serving those markets that demand speed and reliability for the transport of goods. Cargo can either be transported on dedicated commercial air freighters or in the belly of passenger planes.

indexes.title: BAI
indexes.description:
The Baltic Air Freight Index reflects transacted rates from key hubs: London, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Chicago, Shanghai and Singapore to the main import regions globally.

The indices include six outbound indices and 17 individual destination baskets and are priced in US$/kg.

segments.title: Dry
segments.description:
Shipping Type

The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) is the successor to the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) and came into operation on 1 November 1999. Since 1 March 2018, the index is a weighted average of the Capesize 40pct, Panamax 30pct and Supramax 30pct Timecharter Averages which is then multiplied by a multiplier of 0.1.

Additionally the Baltic also publishes a Handysize index which is not included in the BDI calculation.

indexes.title: BCI
indexes.description:
Sector



Capesize vessels are large sized gearless dry bulk carriers. They typically range between 130,000 – 210,000 deadweight tonnage (DWT). Cargoes for Capesize vessels are limited to iron ore, coal and bauxite while port infrastructure requires ample draft and strength to hold the larger vessels. Capesize vessels have historically been restricted from passing through major canals due to their size, forcing the vessels to transit via the Cape of Good Hope or Cape Horn, hence the  name "Capesize".

segments.title: Containers
segments.description:
Shipping Type

The Freightos Baltic Global Container Index (FBX) reflects the price of a 40-foot container shipped on 12 key international tradelanes. 

Standard containers tend to be described as either twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) or forty-foot equivalent units (FEU) and can be transported by container ship, truck and freight trains as part of a single journey without unpacking.  They are commonly used to transport a range of finished goods or bulk commodities.  Specialist containers are also used to transport perishable goods and liquids.
